column1: # LAB-ONLY. HELD ROWS of the INVIOLABLE workload rule (validation/wl_verdict.py; WL-DYNAMIC-GATE, owner ruling #6965,
# 2026-11-20; D-X.141). The rule binds the dynamic kit: each workload at or below 1.10x glibc in instructions:u and in
# page faults, geomean of instructions:u at or below 1.00. A row here was over 1.10x when the rule moved to the
# dynamic kit, for the cause it names; it is bounded at `level` (libniji / glibc, the ratio recorded on next, rounded
# up to 4 decimals) instead of 1.10. A RATCHET: a level is never raised and a row is never added for a CPU class
# already recorded (wl_verdict.py holds, run by validation/wl_verdict_test.sh against the merge base). A row that
# measures at or below 1.10x drops its hold in that run (HOLD-RELEASE): remove it (wl_verdict.py check --update).
# cpu = /proc/cpuinfo "model name" of the count host (instructions follow the IFUNC variant a CPU selects); glibc and
# libniji = the recorded counts, the WORST observed so a rerun of next does not exceed the level (a level a rerun can
# exceed is a flake), from a wl_count run whose BASE column is next: instructions:u the base column's mean and glibc's
# mean; page faults the highest single base run and the lowest glibc run (the log's "faults min..max" line); recorded =
# the measured next head and date. `level` must equal ceil4(libniji / glibc) of its own row (wl_verdict.py holds
# recomputes it: a level edited without its counts is refused).
# D-X.151 (WL-COUNT-HONEST-CHEAP, 2026-11-21): a count's page faults are now the lowest of 5 runs under setarch -R. gzip-c's
# hold is dropped (next measures 292 / 269 = 1.0855 in every count, so the 1.10 bound binds).
# D-X.155 (WL-LEVELS-RERECORD, 2026-11-21): every measured run now gets one fixed environment (validation/wl_stats.sh
# WL_RUN_ENV under env -i), and every level below was re-recorded from 5 counts of next 0299fd6e1 on the Zen 1 host in
# it, libniji (new and base columns) and glibc both measured fresh: libniji = the highest of the 10 libniji columns,
# glibc = the lowest of the 5 glibc columns (page faults: each column the lowest of its 5 runs; printf-loop, a 25-minute
# row, from 2 of the counts). Single-process rows repeat exactly over the 5 counts. The levels recorded before (189ab9cbc) had glibc page-fault numbers the fixed
# environment does not reproduce (sed-s 251 against 212 measured; every row's glibc fell by 0 to 39), so rows rise or
# fall: a rise is a CORRECTION under the owner's ruling of 2026-11-21 ("accurate results are more important"), never
# a loosening, and is accepted only with `correction D-X.<n>` in its cause, a new `recorded` and a libniji count not
# above the one before (libniji did not get worse; glibc's number was wrong). tar-gz (a 4 s two-process pipeline): 2
# of its 10 libniji columns had every run 110+ faults above the rest (758, 765: positive excursions as in D-X.151);
# its libniji is the highest of the other 8 (629..647).
